We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}-6 & 7 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & 7{\alpha }_{1}t \\ -2{\alpha }_{1}t & 3{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues of $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=-4t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=t,
$$

both of multiplicity one. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}r(-4t)={e}^{-4t} \\ r(t)={e}^{t}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}-4t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{-4t} \\ t{\alpha }_{1}+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{t}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

- Subtraction the second equation from the first one, we get

$$
-5t{\alpha }_{1}={e}^{-4t}-{e}^{t}\,⇒\,{\alpha }_{1}=-\frac{1}{5t}({e}^{-4t}-{e}^{t}).
$$

- Multiplying the second equation by $4$ and adding to the first one, we get

$$
5{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{-4t}+4{e}^{t}\,⇒\,{\alpha }_{0}=\frac{1}{5}({e}^{-4t}+4{e}^{t}).
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =6(-\frac{1}{5t}({e}^{-4t}-{e}^{t}))t+\frac{1}{5}({e}^{-4t}+4{e}^{t}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}((-6{e}^{-4t}+6{e}^{t}))+({e}^{-4t}+4{e}^{t})) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(7{e}^{-4t}-2{e}^{t}) \\ -2{\alpha }_{1}t & =-2(-\frac{1}{5t}({e}^{-4t}-{e}^{t}))t \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2{e}^{-4t}-2{e}^{t})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}7{e}^{-4t}-2{e}^{t} & -7{e}^{-4t}+7{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-4t}-2{e}^{t} & -2{e}^{-4t}+7{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$
